# 32-bit mode snippets, separated by `=== <name>`, checked against GNU as.
# Alignment padding is left out, as in programs.txt: GNU as picks its no-ops
# by -mtune.

=== short branches both ways
back:
    nop
    jmp back
    jne fwd
    call back
fwd:
    ret

=== branches that need the long form
    jmp far
    je far
    jb far
    .space 200
far:
    jg 1f
    .space 130
1:  ret

=== a branch just in range of the short form
    jmp 1f
    .space 127
1:  jmp 2f
    .space 128
2:  ret

=== counter branches
1:  loop 1b
    loope 1b
    loopne 1b
    jecxz 1b
    jcxz 1b
    jecxz 2f
    nop
2:  ret

=== local addresses as data and displacements
    movl $msg, %eax
    leal msg(%ebx), %ecx
    movl msg, %edx
    movw $msg, %ax
    pushl $msg
    .long msg, msg - ., . - msg
    .word msg - start
msg:
    .ascii "hi"
start:
    ret

=== a far jump and call to a local label
    ljmp $0x08, $target
    lcall $0x10, $target
    ljmpw $0x18, $target
target:
    lret

=== intel syntax: labels are memory unless offset is written
    .intel_syntax noprefix
    mov eax, value
    mov eax, offset value
    lea ecx, value
    push offset value
    push value
    jmp next
next:
    call next
value:
    .long 1

=== intel syntax: far pointers and string operands
    .intel_syntax noprefix
    jmp 0x10:0x2000
    call 0x20:there
    movs byte ptr es:[edi], byte ptr fs:[esi]
    rep stos dword ptr es:[edi]
there:
    retf

=== 16-bit code in a 32-bit file
    .code16
    jmp 1f
    jmp 2f
1:  je 2f
    call 1b
    .space 300
2:  movw $1, %ax
    movl $1, %eax
    .code32
    movw $1, %ax
    movl $1, %eax

=== 16-bit branches that need the long form
    .code16
    jmp far16
    jne far16
    jcxz near16
    .space 100
near16:
    .space 100
far16:
    loop near16
    ret

=== code16gcc widens the stack to 32 bits
    .code16gcc
    push %eax
    push $1
    pushl %ds
    pusha
    pushf
    call 1f
1:  ret
    leave
    lret
    popf
    popa
    pop %ebx
    iret
    jmp *(%bx)
    .code16
    push $1
    call 1b
    ret

=== x87 register stack operations in sequence
    fld1
    fldpi
    faddp
    fldz
    fxch %st(1)
    fsub %st, %st(1)
    fsubr %st(1), %st
    fdivp %st, %st(1)
    fstps (%esp)
    fcomip %st(1), %st
    fcmovne %st(1), %st
    ffreep %st(0)
